transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-23 14:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Liao (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (Redwood CSM); Priya Shah (Solstice Head of ML), Tom Korey (Eng Manager), Mei Chen (SRE), Alex Rivera (Procurement)

AUTO SUMMARY (auto-generated) — Solstice is evaluating a 12-month Dedicated commit to reduce unit cost and secure capacity for a planned Q2 rollout. Key concerns: peak tail latency in heavy bursts, audit log retention, and ability to fallback to hosted during maintenance windows.

[00:00] Jamie Liao: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we've got Priya, Tom, Mei, Alex on the Solstice side, and Carlos and Aisha with me. We're aiming for a 60 minute check-in, mostly to align on capacity and risk.
[00:22] Priya Shah: Hi, hi. Thanks Jamie. We've been looking at the usage reports you sent — thanks for that — had a few follow-ups on the peak shapes.
[00:30] Carlos Mendes: Quick note — I pulled the batch/tokens breakdown, saw a lot of short chat-like requests but the top 5 templates generate long continuations, which drives token variance. I'll share the breakdown.
[01:05] Tom Korey: To frame it, our product team wants a committed pool for predictable latency during launches. Our main question is — what commitment gives us good economics without overpaying for idle time?
[01:30] Aisha Patel: And from CS perspective, we've seen the billing spikes on the monthly report — we'll walk through a right-size exercise today.

Topics: commitment tiers, SLA tradeoffs, private VPC options, KV cache usage.

[06:12] Mei Chen: On SRE side, we care about tail latency. During the Oct promo, 99.9th jumped from 420ms to 1.8s in a 30 minute window. That is what we want to avoid.
[06:40] Jamie Liao: Thanks Mei. That's consistent with the telemetry we saw; bursts are often due to concurrent long-context requests. Two levers: 1) reserved Dedicated pool with higher concurrency, and 2) caching + batching to smooth tokens.
[07:15] Priya Shah: If we go Dedicated, what's the fallback if a node needs maintenance? We can't have user-facing timeouts.
[07:32] Carlos Mendes: Good Q. Redwood supports automatic fallback to hosted variants or to a GPU pool in another region; you can configure canary/fallback rules per route. There is a brief reconnection time — typically sub-500ms for reroutes but stateful sessions need KV warming.
[08:05] Tom Korey: Does that reconnection break the KV cache? We rely on a KV cache for conversation context.
[08:18] Carlos Mendes: If the routing moves to a different model variant or different machine, the KV cache won't carry automatically. We recommend persisting prefix context in your app or using Redwood's session prefetching to warm cache. We also have sticky routing options for session affinity.

[12:45] Alex Rivera: Procurement question — can we get a committed capacity contract that allows burst credits? Our usage is spiky and fixed commit looks risky.
[12:58] Jamie Liao: Yes, we offer burst credits on top of committed pools; there are configurable burst bands (10–50% depending on tier) and pre-purchased burst tokens are an option. We'll include sample tiers in the pricing doc.

[16:03] Priya Shah: Security check — we need SOC2 type II evidence, audit logs for model inputs for 180 days, and KMS integration. Does Redwood support on-prem KMS/HSM?
[16:22] Aisha Patel: Redwood supports both cloud KMS integrations and HSM options for private deployments. Audit logs can be exported to your SIEM and retention extended. We'll attach our security pack but wanted to confirm any gap.
[16:45] Mei Chen: Do we get per-request redaction or field-level masking before logs are stored?
[16:56] Carlos Mendes: We have pre-processing hooks and function-calls/transformers so you can scrub PII before it's persisted. Some customers use the edge transform or your own sidecar. We'll share examples.

[21:10] Tom Korey: On numbers — our average tokens per request is ~420, but the variance is huge. We saw a 3x increase in peak windows. If we commit to a 2x headroom, that might be too expensive. How would you model the tiers?
[21:36] Jamie Liao: We typically present 3 tiers: conservative (commit ~1.1x current 90th), balanced (1.5x 95th), aggressive (2x 95th with burst). Each tier includes projected monthly spend, expected % token discount vs hosted, and recommended autoscale policies.
[22:05] Priya Shah: Can we get a spreadsheet with month-by-month burn and example autoscale curves?
[22:12] Aisha Patel: Yes, we'll send a burn model and an example autoscaler set of rules tuned for latency SLOs.

[26:40] Jamie Liao: Quick demo note — Carlos, can you show the KV cache warm strategy?
[26:47] Carlos Mendes: Sure, short demo: if you persist session prefix in Redis and call the prefetch endpoint, the runtime will populate KV quickly. That reduces cold-starts by about 70% in our priors. I'll attach the snippet.
[27:23] Priya Shah: That's promising. Do you have any guidance for very large context windows? We have long documents for some flows.
[27:35] Carlos Mendes: For long contexts, chunking + retrieval works best: keep active context in KV and offload full documents to embeddings+vector store. Also, quantized variants can help on Dedicated to reduce memory pressure.

[31:18] Mei Chen: Risk scenario — if region A loses capacity, how quickly can we failover to region B without violating latency SLO?
[31:30] Jamie Liao: There's an inherent tradeoff. If you want sub-200ms global failover, you need geo-proximate pools and warm caches in both regions. Otherwise allow a few seconds of degraded latency but preserve correctness. We'll outline options with estimated RTOs.

[36:02] Alex Rivera: On contractual terms — is there a minimum annual commit? We prefer flexibility: maybe quarterly true-ups instead of an annual lock.
[36:15] Jamie Liao: We can do 12 month standard, but we have 6- and 3-month pilots with escalated unit pricing and option to convert credits to a longer-term commitment with a rebate. We'll include both a 3-month pilot scenario and a 12-month commitment in the proposal.

[40:55] Priya Shah: Technical acceptance criteria for us: 99th latency under 500ms for typical chat flows, ability to retain audit trail for 180 days, and the ability to run a load test that replicates the Oct promo.
[41:12] Carlos Mendes: Noted — we can run the load test jointly; we recommend a phased test: baseline, 1.5x, 2x traffic, and then degradation window. We'll schedule with your infra team.

[45:30] Tom Korey: Any surprising constraints from your side? For example, GPU types, quantization support, or model variants that don't support KV?
[45:42] Carlos Mendes: Most modern open models support KV cache. The main constraints are custom kernels for quantized weights — some 4-bit kernels have slight differences but we validate per-model. If you need specific model parity we can run a quick regression.

[49:10] Priya Shah: For cost modeling — do you show the per-token effective price with and without batching? Because batching helps a lot, and our average batch size right now is one.
[49:28] Aisha Patel: We do show unit economics with typical batching improvements. There's a recommended client-side small change to allow micro-batching which can drop per-token cost by 20–35% depending on request shape. Carlos will include sample SDK changes.

[53:05] Jamie Liao: Recap before we close — action items and timeline. We'll send: 1) Dedicated pricing tiers + sample contract 2) Burn model spreadsheet with autoscale examples 3) KV cache + batching best-practices 4) Security pack + SOC2 artifacts. You (Solstice) will return sample traffic, top prompts, and preferred test dates.

[54:00] Priya Shah: Sounds good. One more operational: what's the onboarding time for Dedicated pool? We need to plan calendar impacts.
[54:12] Aisha Patel: Typical onboarding from signed contract to pool provisioning is 4–6 weeks, shorter if you take our standard configs. Pilot options can be spun up inside 5–7 business days for a limited pool.

[57:40] Alex Rivera: Procurement question — any flexibility on initial billing cadence? Net-30 or Net-45?
[57:50] Jamie Liao: Standard is Net-30, but for enterprise deals we can discuss Net-45 or milestone-based invoicing with legal. We'll surface options in the proposal.

[60:05] Mei Chen: Ok — we'll aim to share the traffic snapshot and preliminary decision by next Tuesday.
[60:18] Priya Shah: And we'll propose load test windows for early December.
[60:30] Jamie Liao: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs + pricing by Friday.

END OF TRANSCRIPT
